title: Smoking hop, gambling and an arrest
summary: Users once kept to themselves; Wilson never used drugs and was jailed for running a poker game after refusing to buy beer in a white bar.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: But did they smoke hop in those times? Well, yes.

But you see, a man smoke hop, he stayed to himself. A man used dope, he stayed to himself. He didn't bum all together like they do today. If you was a dope addict, you had your bunch. And like I knew, when you used dope, well why didn't it associate with you at all? But now they're all together, you don't know who's who. I remember when you could get a moot of cigarette, two for fifteen. That's right. Two for fifteen?

Two for fifteen. And that was the only thing that I was out there at R.S. Chandler. And I know the fellas that handled that stuff. Now we'd be around a poker table playing poker, and the fellas would walk in there and send somebody out to, and get a dozen. I'd be on the table. I'd smoke them like that on the table. I'd never smoke one in my life. They used to tell me to light it. I'd take a match and hold it up this way. If it lights or if it didn't light, I'd never run my mouth for life. And they fellas say, well you bummed out that much drunk. Why you didn't? Well I didn't, I don't know. I never did pick up a bad habit. I never had a fight in my life. That's the truth. I didn't, I was a, I don't know, I just wanted to be a good fella. I never did like to do nothing bad. And if fellas were going to do something bad, he said, you stay in love with something bad. I'm with some bad boys. And they fellas say, well you bummed out that much drunk. Why you didn't? Well I didn't, I don't know, I never did pick up a bad habit. I never was a drunker. I never had a fight in my life. That's the truth. I didn't, I was a, I don't know, I just wanted to be a good fella. I never did like to do nothing bad. And if fellas were going to do something bad, he said, you stay in love with something bad. I was a bad boy. I never went to jail in my life. I wasn't going to be gambling. I went to jail many times in the region, the region, the giant book of gambling. Yeah. But outside of that, I never went to jail. Police never stopped me. I was sitting on the corner and the police walked up there hard, I'll never forget. And they wanted me to go, that's the during the time that they really segregated bars and so on. And they wanted me to go about three blocks and buy a beer. Well, the old man would have sold me the beer and I could have drank it in there. Not me, but the wrong person. But he got a father doing it. And went there and put the old man in jail. He said, no. He said, no. He says, so he asked, did they go run the place? I said, what did they say? The dagger told me, he's all right. He told him, he said, no, you're going to get that far. I do nothing like that. He said, not him. He ain't going to do that. He won't do that. He said, no, you're going to get that far. Because he put me in jail. Because he put me in jail. I told him what they put me in jail for. That's what he put me in jail for. I wasn't probably in no laws. And I was running the classic game, you see. I was running the poker game too. Because I didn't go down there and buy a beer in that white place. You going to put me in jail for that? So I told him, no, he said, he's all right. Don't worry about him. He's all right.
